text:
Maria: FYI — this morning eu-west spot GPU pool had a ~18m preemption surge that hit batch inference. ~25% of running jobs failed before we could reschedule.
Sam: yikes. any quick logs?
Maria: provider termination notice present on nodes. CA spun up nodes in other pools but scheduler wouldn't place pods because of taint/affinity mismatch.
Yuki: we use taint gpu=type:NoSchedule and set nodeAffinity to prefer spot values. Seems fallback pool uses gpu=reserved which blocked placement.
Kevin: so CA did scale, but scheduler denied placement. two ways to fix: (A) make fallback pools tolerable for spot workloads (tolerations + relaxed affinity) or (B) standardize taint keys so pools differ by value only.
devops-bot: Incident logged: INC-20260318-009 1 assigned Sam
Sam: short-term mitigation: patched batch Job spec to accept nodeAffinity OR terms for gpu=spot OR gpu=reserved and added toleration for gpu=reserved. also added degraded CPU-quantized replica as soft fallback.
Maria: implemented a local preempt handler DaemonSet on nodes to detect termination notice and cordon+evict small jobs to reduce lost work. snippet:
```
# node-side preempt watcher (pseudo)
if curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/spot/termination-time; then
  kubectl cordon "$NODE"
  kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName="$NODE" -o name | xargs -n1 -P4 kubectl evict --grace-period=30
fi
```
Maria: this moves short-lived tasks to warm standby faster than waiting for CA to reprovision compatible nodes.
Carmen: long-term thought: prewarm tiny reserved pool (2x T4) per region as hot-standby. cost vs reliability tradeoff.
Praveen: rough cost math: 2 T4 reserved ~ $0.30/hr in eu-west. If it avoids ~150 failed jobs/day during peak, ROI looks <10 days when factoring SLA penalties.
Yuki: proposed Ops actions: 1) standardize taint key to gpu=type with values spot|reserved and allow tolerations for both; 2) update CA config to include fallback pools in scale decisions and mark them as compatible; 3) deploy preemption-notice DaemonSet (cordon+evict); 4) add alert: batch failure rate >10% over 5m; 5) canary CPU-quantized fallback.
Maria: I'll open PRs for CA mapping + taint standardization and a DaemonSet for the notice handler. plan to roll at 22:00 UTC tonight (low traffic). any objections?
Kevin: +1. also add runbook steps to manually evict with --grace-period=120 and a procedure to promote reserved pool capacity.
Sam: I'll own the incident update, link the PRs, and add Grafana panels: batch-failures-by-pool and preemption-heatmap by zone.
Maria: Thanks all 1 will post PR links and rollout checklist when ready :thumbsup:
